key_insight: The paper proposes a hardware-agnostic three-layer architecture that cleanly separates application logic, fault-tolerance functions, and physical execution for scalable quantum computing.
engineering_relevance: It offers a unified systems blueprint for building modular fault-tolerant quantum software stacks across different qubit platforms and error-correction codes.
method: Defines three layers: application, fault-tolerance, and hardware execution.
Breaks the middle fault-tolerance layer into five interacting components with explicit interfaces and data flow.
Maps execution, correction, and adaptation paths to support logical synthesis, resource management, decoding, and runtime control.
evidence_signal: The abstract indicates a conceptual architecture paper with a full-stack end-to-end example, rather than a results-driven evaluation on benchmark data.
watch_item: As a high-level abstract framework, practical adoption will depend on how well the interfaces can be standardized across diverse hardware and QEC implementations.
paper_title: A Three-Layer Architecture for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
